A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELT research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet image-generation and UCF-101 video-generation experiments, including ELT performance, scaling, throughput and ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds training-resource measurements, loss ablations and loop-update analysis in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The recurrent architecture, stochastic student sampling, teacher stop-gradient, loss curriculum and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. ELTopt introduces an implementation optimization through layer unrolling, without changing the stated learning or inference algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-conditional ImageNet 256×256 image generation and UCF-101 video generation. The added diagnostics introduce no new dataset, task or input-environment scenario.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 13 adds the explicitly labeled 'ELT (multi-exit)' control alongside 'Just Looping' and 'ELT (all losses)' for diffusion and masked generation. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include matched-depth TPU v6e training profiling using step time and peak HBM, additional loss-control configurations, and median L2 feature-update measurements across 512 denoising steps. Existing benchmark settings and configuration Tables 5–7 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B substantially expands the diagnostic analyses beyond v1's scaling and with/without-ILSD comparisons. Figure 13 tests full-loss ELT against a multi-exit control, Figure 14 examines refinement across loops and denoising steps, and Table 8 separates training costs of baseline, looping, ILSD and optimized execution.

E5.justification: The existing UCF-101 uncertainty reporting is retained. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure for its new experiments.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values remain unchanged, while Appendix B adds supporting results. Table 8 reports baseline/ELT/ELTopt step times of 130/130/118 ms and peak-HBM values of 7.7/5.1/5.8. Figures 13–14 add loss-control FID curves and loop-update trends, rather than improved scores for the retained benchmarks.

T1.justification: The transformer-composition definitions, ILSD objectives and sampling-temperature equation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or mathematical derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: parameter-efficient visual generation, any-time inference from one training run, and predictable scaling. The headline fourfold parameter reduction, ImageNet FID 2.0 and UCF-101 FVD 72.8 are unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 explains efficiency through up to L-fold higher arithmetic intensity and discusses using memory savings for faster execution. Appendix B connects the observed update patterns to potential adaptive loop allocation across denoising steps. The existing failure cases and deployment limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents ELTopt's explicit layer unrolling instead of jax.lax.scan and identifies the TPU v6e configuration used for training profiling. Earlier hyperparameter tables, sampling details and pseudocode remain intact.

R1.justification: V3 adds DC-DiT to the elastic-generation discussion and removes the citation to Randomized Autoregressive Visual Generation. Most positioning is retained. Moving related work, updating Matformer's publication details and consolidating duplicate latent-diffusion references do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A to Section 2, subsequent sections are renumbered, and an Additional Experiments appendix is introduced. There are limited prose and correspondence edits; most method, results and conclusion text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 8 and Figures 13–14, redraws Figure 6, and adds baseline-configuration cross-references to Figures 4–5. Existing qualitative figures and implementation tables are repositioned or grouped differently, while their underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Figure 13 provides a useful control for assessing what full-loss training adds beyond multi-exit training, Table 8 directly measures training costs, and Figure 14 supports the refinement discussion. These additions improve empirical support and transparency, although their brief descriptions leave some implementation and measurement details unspecified.
